title: What is IELTS?

display.layout: hero + purpose tiles + recognitions + background accordion

highlights.heading: The name
highlights.text: IELTS stands for International English Language Testing System. It is the world's most widely recognized high-stakes English language assessment, trusted by over 12,500 organizations globally.
bullets: Global benchmark: Established to assess English language proficiency for study, work, and migration.
Origins and history: Launched in 1980 (initially as ELTS) and restructured into the international partnership in 1989.
Joint ownership: Co-owned by the British Council, IDP: IELTS Australia, and Cambridge University Press & Assessment.

highlights.heading: Four language skills
highlights.text: The test measures Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking to ensure candidates can communicate effectively in English-speaking academic and professional environments.
bullets: Comprehensive assessment: Assesses both receptive skills (listening and reading comprehension) and productive skills (writing and live interactive speech).
Section scoring: Each individual section receives a band score from 0 to 9, which combines into an overall composite band score.
Communicative validity: Questions simulate authentic language tasks encountered in higher education, workplaces, and daily life.

highlights.heading: Why people take it
highlights.text: IELTS is taken by millions of candidates worldwide each year to unlock academic opportunities, advance global careers, or fulfill immigration and visa requirements.
bullets: University admissions: Required by undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral degree programs across English-speaking countries.
Immigration and visas: Used by government departments in the UK, Australia, Canada, and New Zealand for skilled worker, permanent residency, and student visas.
Professional licensing: Required by regulatory boards in healthcare (doctors, nurses, pharmacists), accounting, engineering, law, and education.

highlights.heading: Recognition
highlights.text: Over 12,500 institutions, governments, employers, and professional registration bodies worldwide recognize IELTS results as dependable evidence of English ability.
bullets: Global reach: Accepted across more than 140 countries worldwide, including all universities in Australia and New Zealand, over 3,400 US institutions, and all UK universities.
Electronic verification: Receiving institutions verify candidate Test Report Forms (TRFs) directly and securely via the centralized IELTS verification service.
Employment credentials: Demonstrates proven international communication capability to multinational employers in finance, aviation, energy, hospitality, and tech.

highlights.heading: Requirements vary
highlights.text: There is no single pass or fail score in IELTS. Each university, employer, or government department establishes its own minimum band score criteria.
bullets: Institution criteria: Score requirements reflect the language demands of the specific course of study or professional occupation.
Component minimums: Many universities require not only an overall band (e.g. Band 6.5 or 7.0) but also minimum individual sub-scores in Writing or Speaking.
Verify before booking: Always check the exact IELTS version (Academic, General Training, or UKVI) and score profile demanded by your target institution before registering.

highlights.heading: Partners
highlights.text: IELTS is jointly managed by three distinguished organizations with extensive expertise in education, testing research, and international cultural relations.
bullets: British Council: The UK's international organization for educational and cultural relations, delivering IELTS across hundreds of test centres in over 140 countries.
IDP: IELTS Australia: Global education services provider operating in over 50 countries, administering IELTS testing and student placement services globally.
Cambridge University Press & Assessment: World leader in language assessment, responsible for test development, research validation, question design, and grading rubrics.
